title: Rootstock
what: The roots your Variety is grafted onto, bred mostly from American vine species. They resist phylloxera and decide how the vine copes with lime, drought and vigour; own-rooted vines skip grafting but have no protection against the louse.

steps: A thin, stony soil holding little water
dries out sooner for shallow-rooted 3309C than for deep-rooted 1103 Paulsen
severe water stress closes the stomata
so sugar loading stalls in a dry summer

choose: Read the soil first. Lime: Fercal tolerates a chlorosis index up to 120, SO4 and 1103 Paulsen about 30, 3309C only 10. Drought: 1103 Paulsen roots deep and tolerates it; 3309C does not. Cool, moist sites: low-vigour, early-ripening 3309C helps ripening.
exam: Expect 'why graft?' or 'pick a rootstock for chalky or dry soil'. Answer soil or pest → root trait → vine → grape, with a real example.

check.question: A Côte d'Or Block has marl with a chlorosis index of about 40 and a deep, moist soil. Which rootstock fits?
options: 1103 Paulsen, because drought tolerance comes first
Own-rooted, since grafting is unnecessary on limestone
check.why: An index of 40 is beyond what 3309C (10), SO4 and 1103 Paulsen (30) tolerate, so they would turn yellow; Fercal copes up to 120. Water is no constraint on a deep, moist soil, and own-rooted vines lack phylloxera resistance.

simplification: Game simplification: the game turns active lime into a chlorosis index assuming the same soil iron everywhere (index ≈ 4 × lime %), so rootstocks yellow at lower lime than published tables give (3309C about 11 %, SO4 and 1103 Paulsen about 17 % active lime). Phylloxera on own-rooted vines is only a warning in the game.
